data.one_liner: Detect visible items and select one stable primary item in Flutter scrollables.
data.what_it_does: Scroll_spy measures item positions in scrollable viewports, determines which items intersect a configurable attention region, and selects a single stable primary item using customizable policies and anti-flicker stability rules. It exposes granular notifiers for visibility, focus, and primary winner states without requiring manual geometry math.
use_when: You are building a video feed that needs autoplay for exactly one visible card at a time.
You need to highlight reading position or table of contents items based on viewport focus.
Multiple items are visible and you need hysteresis and anti-flicker rules to prevent rapid switching.
avoid_when: You only need basic visibility percentages for individual widgets without choosing a single primary winner.
Your application targets SDKs older than Flutter 3.47.7 and Dart 3.13.5.
strengths: O(1) position derivation during steady scrolling using a cached scroll model without render-tree walks.
Built-in stability rules like hysteresis and minimum primary duration to prevent UI flickering.
Granular, lazy, and diff-optimized notifiers for high scroll performance.
weaknesses: Requires updating to Flutter 3.47.7+ and Dart 3.13.5+ for version 2.0.0.
Adds overhead compared to raw visibility checks if you only need simple widget visibility reporting.
